Name: C++ UIKit
ShortDescription: A C++ library for making quick and simple console UIs.
Description: This was a fun project I worked on to help me prototype console tools quicker and allow me to make them look and feel nice. I worked on it from Sept 2020 to Feb 2021. It was made for windows, and while some features might work on other operating systems a few will certainly not, such as the cursor menu.Full documentation is available as well as a demo application that showcases many of the features. You can find both of those things on the Github Repo.

Name: Epsi's Den
ShortDescription: The website you're on right now!
Description:
This is the all new version of my website, V3, with custom styling and C# backend tools for making post and project pages from markdown. I've also massively redone my Music Recommendations page to showcase my recommendations better, with better links to listen to them, and more backend tools in C# to quickly add and manage recommendations.

There are also some easter eggs to find, like a hidden page.

Name: Discord Data Package Explorer
ShortDescription: A simple way to view the data inside your discord data package.
Description:
This is a small little application to view the information stored in a Discord Data Package. This is to help users easily explore the data discord has on them, as it can be hard for normal users to comb through large text and json files.

You can find the code and application downloads on GitHub

Update: Pushed v1.0.1 to fix an odd COM related crash in newer Win11 versions.

Name: E621 C# Library
ShortDescription: A wrapper around many of the e621.net api endpoints.
Description:
This was made while I was learning REST API development for the first time. I picked the e621 API for the funny and because it’s auth and rate-limits were relaxed and easy to start with. This later went on to be used in Fluff, which was my first attempt at a good looking UI application. I hosted it on nuget to make it easier to use in my projects, and for some reason it has 11k+ downloads xP

You can find the code on GitHub and the built library on nuget. Documentation for this is incomplete and I’ll likely not revisit it!

Name: FFTVIS
ShortDescription: A file format that stores a pre generated frequency spectrum for visualizing audio files.
Description:
The FFTVIS file format is a compacted representation of a pre generated frequency spectrum for visualizing audio files. It's a simple format at it's base: a header describing the generation and how to play it back properly, and an array of arrays of doubles from 0->1 representing the amplitude of a frequency bin. It supports 3 extra encoding steps for compression: ZSTD 3, Delta Encoding, and Quantization (to 16 or 8 bit). Check out the Blog Post for more info about the development of this project! 

This project was a bitch and a blast to work on haha. I love visualizing data and audio always looks so cool. Currently FFTVIS Version 2 supports Normalized, Mel, and Log10 representations of the audio spectrum in mono. In the future, I'd love to try and extend a version 3 with support for dual channel frames for left and right audio spectrum visualizations, and since bin mapping can be swapped out for any function, I'd like to add support to the library for setting custom bin maps sometime soon. But I've been working my ass off for this and done lots of research and writing, and I can't scope creep forever if I want this to ever release xP

Extra Notes:
Version 2 was the release version. Version 1 used grouped compression stages, so you could only select None, Zstd, Zstd+Quant, Zstd+Quant+Deltas. Version 2 moved to a bitmask to enable toggling,

The library doesn't have explicit support for swapping to a custom bin map, but the file format is agnostic to it. If you were to edit the library or build your own custom frame builder, as long as you save it out the way the format expects it (frames of 0-1) then it should work just fine.

You should really try to lock your timer to the audio player's position. Attempting to run two timers in sync will just be a pain in ass.

FFT Values of more 32k+, unless using audio with a high sample rate (88, 96, 129), will not look correct. This is because it takes up too much time inside each frame, averaging too much of the song at once to be accurate to the audio being played at that moment.

Name: Fluff
Description:
A beautiful, native windows app for e926/e621! View, search, and download posts submitted by other users, and submit your own.

This was a fun project I used to deep dive into learning UWP and making better UIs. It got pretty far along, but I’ll likely no longer be updating it. It does still mostly work despite a few bugs, I may go fix them at some point but I don’t plan to. I’m pretty proud of the result, especially the custom control behavior I made for the upload page.

If you want to check this out, it’s available on GitHub and the Microsoft Store. Don’t worry, it starts in safe mode! You have to enable NSFW content in the settings if that’s what you’re looking for :P

Name: FreakFreq
ShortDescription: A super customizable audio visualizer for windows!
Description:
FreqFreak is an application made in WPF that can take in audio from WASAPI loopback for output, input, and per process id and show it with pretty and customizable audio visualizations. Tons of options, multiple built in bin mappings, easy saving/loading of config files, and many color/size/shape customizations for the spectrum. This was a labor of love as someone who grew up placing visualizers into my desktop backgrounds using Rainmeter way back in the day. As Rainmeter seems to be mostly out of fashion and many of it's popular visualizers now being broken or dead in some way, I wanted a new way to make visualizations on my PC. You can read more about the dev process and the how it works on the Blog Post! It's all free, as is it's codebase. Feel free to add / fix things or use it to build up your own visualizing systems :D

Changelog:
v2.0.13
- Fixed a regression in Photo Cutouts (I fixed a bug and then managed to merge it back in)
- Some PCs experienced a flicker in gradient settings, this should be fixed now!


v2.0.12 (GitHub Only Release)
- You can now toggle pitch + frequency peak tracking
- Fixed Outer Circle and Inner Circle modes not showing peaks unless in stereo mode.

v2.0.11
- The AudioDevices window crash due to a weak reference to it's Dispatcher has been fixed
- The Lines in centered mode were being drawn incorrectly on the right side with 2 stray points, these points are now gone
- The Cutouts can now use the arrow keys for nudging just like the main Visualizer.
- PathGeometry Memory Leak fixed
- Line Brush Memory Leak fixed
- Color system is now more performant

v2.0.10
- Dual Channel visualizations 
    - Add Left Channel/Right Channel/Stereo/Mono selector 
    - Add Oscilloscope Visualization (Stereo Mode only) 
    - Stereo Mode for Centered
    - Stereo Mode for Inner/Outer Circle
- Add Pitch Tracking + Color effect 
    - Current Pitch Guess + Note Guess + Peak Frequency Guess in the Options Window
    - Pitch color modes show the current pitch guess as a color on the gradient between color 1-2 or a rainbow gradient.
    - Frequency color modes show the current frequency peak guess as a color on the gradient between color 1-2 or a rainbow gradient.
    - Pitch/Peak guess is ONLY SEMI ACURATE, and can become more or less accurate depending on your FFT settings. It is also based off a mono representation of the audio in stereo mode, although in left/right exclusive modes it will base of the specified channel.
- Revamped Color Modes
    - Single Color 
    - Dual Color Gradient Vertical, Horizontal, Height, Pitch, or Frequency
    - Custom N-Color Gradient Vertical, Horizontal, Height, Pitch, or Frequency 
        - To support custom gradients, a new Gradient Editor was added with some presets 
- New Visualization Options + Modes
    - Show As Lines shows the bars as points on a line(s) instead of bars
    - Peaks now have a selector for mode:
        - Off, Peak Bars, Peak Lines, Peak Bars Only, Peak Lines Only
        - Low End Dampen lets you control how much to dampen the bass compared to the rest of the spectrum, since bass can often be overpowering in audio. The new default is 1.17 (from 1 aka no dampening)
    - Bass Reactive Scaling + Bass Reactive Shake
- Tray Icon Additions
    - Open New Instance
    - Quick Import
    - Quick Access to Audio Input Switcher 
    - Pause/Play Visualization
- Options Menu Buttons moved from bottom to top, and a few new buttons added 
    - Play/Pause (Stops the visualizer from getting new audio data)
    - New Instance (Opens a new visualizer instance)
    - Recenter (Brings the visualizer to be centered on the Options Window)
    - Export
    - Import
    - Audio Input Settings
    - FVZ Tool
    - Cutout Tool
- Cutout Tool lets you place images anywhere on screen
    - Can be used to place images as decoration, or to cover up parts of the screen.
    - For example, cutting out the subject of the desktop background, and placing it's cutout overtop the visualizer, to give it depth.
    - Can also be Bass Reactive
- Optimization Pass
    - Visualizations are now spread out across more threads: 
    - Audio comes in and is built into frames on it's own thread on the CPU, while another CPU threads preps the window and takes those audio frames and turns them into GPU ready frames.
    - The GPU now handles rendering the visuals, improving FPS and making the maximum settings you can get away with larger.
    - The Options Window and it's subsequent windows are now given their own UI threads, instead of piggy backing off of the visualizer's. This means they no longer lock up when the visualizer lags now.
- Audio Switcher can now be refreshed without reopening it
- New Dark + Transparent style 
    - Windows will now try and open out of the way of other FreqFreak Windows (to the top/left/right/bottom)
    - Accent + Tray icon color is now more consistently colorful
- Keyboard nudging (you can use your arrow keys to nudge the selected visualizer window by 1 pixel for precise alignment) 

v1.1.0
- Added a Rotation parameter
- Fixed circle visualizers sizing their canvas oddly
- Added version number to Options UI

Name: Pointer Fishing
ShortDescription: Turn your desktop into an ocean to fish from!
Description: ![Catching a fish](/images/PointerFishingOne.gif){width=50%}In Pointer Fishing, fish will spawn anywhere on your monitor. Grab them with your mouse and they'll take off running, dragging your cursor with them. Fight to keep them within your net to catch them!## BehaviorsFish can have different behaviors that change how they flee from your net. A normal fish will just run away from the net, while floppers kick the net away, confused run in random directions, and anxious fight harder the closer they are to capture. You'll have to adapt to their behavior to keep them in your net.## Fish Fish Fish Fish FishThere are 197 fish across 6 Rarities and 9 themed Locations. Additionally, fish can mutate in 8 different ways, affecting their look and their worth.![Locations](/images/LocationBanner.png)![Rarities](/images/Rarities.png){width=50%}## Bounties and QuestsWith a vast ocean of fish to find, sometimes folks need help getting specific fish. Take on these bounties for specific species, rarities, weights, and variants. Along with paying more per fish, you'll also find Quests which give Gear or Aquarium Items.![Bounty](/images/Bounty.png){width=50%}## Game ModifiersThere are many Modifiers that change your chances and stats. These can make it easier or harder to catch fish and buff or debuff your chances to find certain rarities, mutations, and behaviors. There are many ways to get Modifiers, including gear, changing ocean conditions, and drinks.![Bounty](/images/Modifiers.png){width=50%}## GearEither through the shop, through Fishing, or through Completing Quests, you can obtain Equipable Gear. These items give buffs and debuffs to various stats to help you catch the fish you're looking for, or help you catch fish in general. There are 90 unique Gear to find, but only 2 equipment slots (or 3 after level 100). Mixing gear around depending on other modifiers, location, and daily/weekly condition changes keeps things fresh and gives you more control over gameplay.![Bounty](/images/GearPreview.png){width=50%}## Ocean Conditions![Bounty](/images/OceanConditions.png){width=50%}Daily and Weekly conditions add modifiers to shake up gameplay. 26 Daily and 14 Weekly conditions with various effects, for example:- Blood Moon	- Aggression Chance x2.4	- Erratic Chance x1.8	- Fish Strength x1.12	- Mutation Luck +12- Lazy Day	- Fish Strength x0.86	- Tired Chance x3.5	- Spawn Rate x0.82- Low Tide	- Abyssal Chance x2.4	- Net Size x0.86- Tropical Disturbance	- Luck -14 (In Everblue)	- Mutation Luck +18 (In Everblue)	- Luck -14 (in Avarra)	- Mutation Luck +18 (in Avarra)- Feast or Famine	- Common Chance x3	- Abyssal Chance x2.5	- Tall Tale Chance x2.5## Aquarium ![Bounty](/images/Aquarium.gif){width=50%}If you find a fish you like, you might not want to sell it. With the Aquarium, you can display your favorite fish in a window you can place anywhere on your desktop, or full screen it to let fish roam around your monitor. Fish will swim around according to their Behavior, Floppers bounce off other fish, Erratic Fish randomly boost around, etc. They also react when you click on their window according to their nature, Confused Fish running in a random direction while Aggressive Fish charge at your mouse.In addition to Fish, you'll also find Aquarium items while Fishing or Completing Quests which can be placed within the aquarium window. The floor and background are also customizable with a few presets, and a transparency slider.## LLM Use DisclosureThis project was assisted by LLM tools, used to quickly setup boilerplate code, debug, and optimize code. Every bit of LLM touched code has been manually reviewed by me. Gameplay and much of the main functionality was written by hand by me. All assets, fish sprites, banners, icons, etc were made by humans, either by the wonderful artists of the asset packs listed below, or by myself. ## AttributionI couldn't have completed this project without the work of these artists. [https://happypotato100.itch.io/fishing-icon-pack](https://happypotato100.itch.io/fishing-icon-pack)[https://pixelodyssey.itch.io/100-fish-icons](https://pixelodyssey.itch.io/100-fish-icons)[https://beowulf.itch.io/beowulfs-fish-asset-pack](https://beowulf.itch.io/beowulfs-fish-asset-pack)[https://nrkno.github.io/yr-weather-symbols/](https://nrkno.github.io/yr-weather-symbols/)[https://github.com/Makin-Things/weather-icons](https://github.com/Makin-Things/weather-icons)[https://brysiaa.itch.io/fishtank-pixel-asset-pack-16x16px](https://brysiaa.itch.io/fishtank-pixel-asset-pack-16x16px)[https://ko-fi.com/s/1d57aec437](https://ko-fi.com/s/1d57aec437)[https://kelvira.itch.io/currency-coins-gold-cash-icons](https://kelvira.itch.io/currency-coins-gold-cash-icons)[https://gdainti.itch.io/retro-computer-icons-set-110-icons](https://gdainti.itch.io/retro-computer-icons-set-110-icons)[https://ghostpixxells.itch.io/pixel-mart](https://ghostpixxells.itch.io/pixel-mart)[https://dusk-games.itch.io/dusk-free-ui-icons](https://dusk-games.itch.io/dusk-free-ui-icons)[https://whoga1234.itch.io/freepixelart-magic-book-icons64x6432x32](https://whoga1234.itch.io/freepixelart-magic-book-icons64x6432x32)
DescriptionHtml:
In Pointer Fishing, fish will spawn anywhere on your monitor. Grab them with your mouse and they'll take off running, dragging your cursor with them. Fight to keep them within your net to catch them!

Behaviors

Fish can have different behaviors that change how they flee from your net. A normal fish will just run away from the net, while floppers kick the net away, confused run in random directions, and anxious fight harder the closer they are to capture. You'll have to adapt to their behavior to keep them in your net.

Fish Fish Fish Fish Fish

There are 197 fish across 6 Rarities and 9 themed Locations. Additionally, fish can mutate in 8 different ways, affecting their look and their worth.

Bounties and Quests

With a vast ocean of fish to find, sometimes folks need help getting specific fish. Take on these bounties for specific species, rarities, weights, and variants. Along with paying more per fish, you'll also find Quests which give Gear or Aquarium Items.

Game Modifiers

There are many Modifiers that change your chances and stats. These can make it easier or harder to catch fish and buff or debuff your chances to find certain rarities, mutations, and behaviors. There are many ways to get Modifiers, including gear, changing ocean conditions, and drinks.

Gear

Either through the shop, through Fishing, or through Completing Quests, you can obtain Equipable Gear. These items give buffs and debuffs to various stats to help you catch the fish you're looking for, or help you catch fish in general. There are 90 unique Gear to find, but only 2 equipment slots (or 3 after level 100). Mixing gear around depending on other modifiers, location, and daily/weekly condition changes keeps things fresh and gives you more control over gameplay.

Ocean Conditions

Daily and Weekly conditions add modifiers to shake up gameplay. 26 Daily and 14 Weekly conditions with various effects, for example:

  • Blood Moon
    • Aggression Chance x2.4
    • Erratic Chance x1.8
    • Fish Strength x1.12
    • Mutation Luck +12
  • Lazy Day
    • Fish Strength x0.86
    • Tired Chance x3.5
    • Spawn Rate x0.82
  • Low Tide
    • Abyssal Chance x2.4
    • Net Size x0.86
  • Tropical Disturbance
    • Luck -14 (In Everblue)
    • Mutation Luck +18 (In Everblue)
    • Luck -14 (in Avarra)
    • Mutation Luck +18 (in Avarra)
  • Feast or Famine
    • Common Chance x3
    • Abyssal Chance x2.5
    • Tall Tale Chance x2.5

Aquarium

If you find a fish you like, you might not want to sell it. With the Aquarium, you can display your favorite fish in a window you can place anywhere on your desktop, or full screen it to let fish roam around your monitor. Fish will swim around according to their Behavior, Floppers bounce off other fish, Erratic Fish randomly boost around, etc. They also react when you click on their window according to their nature, Confused Fish running in a random direction while Aggressive Fish charge at your mouse. In addition to Fish, you'll also find Aquarium items while Fishing or Completing Quests which can be placed within the aquarium window. The floor and background are also customizable with a few presets, and a transparency slider.

LLM Use Disclosure

This project was assisted by LLM tools, used to quickly setup boilerplate code, debug, and optimize code. Every bit of LLM touched code has been manually reviewed by me. Gameplay and much of the main functionality was written by hand by me. All assets, fish sprites, banners, icons, etc were made by humans, either by the wonderful artists of the asset packs listed below, or by myself.

Attribution

I couldn't have completed this project without the work of these artists.
